title: He keeps the accounts, so He is all you need
subtitle: Al-Hasib: the Reckoner who misses nothing, and the One who is enough for you
intro: Al-Hasib (الْحسِيبُ) means the Reckoner and the Sufficient: the One who keeps precise account of every deed and will settle it with perfect justice, and the One who is enough for whoever relies on Him. It means you never need to settle every score yourself, and you never lack anything if you have Him.

root.sense: Hisab is counting and reckoning, settling an account. From the same root comes hasb, sufficiency: hasbuka means that is enough for you. Al-Hasib joins both pictures: the One who balances every account exactly, and whose care is so complete that He alone is enough.

row.title: He keeps the account
sub: and He is enough for me

knowing: Al-Hasib is first the Reckoner. He keeps account of all things, even the greeting you return (4:86). On the Day of Judgement the scales of justice will be set up, and even a deed the weight of a mustard seed will be brought out, and He is enough as Reckoner (21:47). {idea}No account with Him is ever rounded off, lost or settled unfairly.{/idea}

Al-Hasib is also the Sufficient. Hasbunallah means Allah is enough for us. Whoever relies on Allah, He is enough for him (65:3). Is Allah not enough for His servant (39:36)? He suffices against enemies, against fear and against need. Two meanings, one truth: because He keeps every account perfectly, nothing that is yours will be lost, and so He really is enough.

How is this different from near names? Al-Muhsi counts and keeps the record of every single thing. Al-Hasib brings that record to account and settles it. Al-Wakil is the One you hand your affairs to. Al-Hasib assures you that once you do, nothing more is needed.
seeing: In verses about the money of orphans, where the weak are easily cheated and no one checks the books, the Quran ends by saying that Allah is enough as Reckoner (4:6). He audits what no human auditor ever sees.

When the believers were told that the people had gathered against them and they should be afraid, it only increased their faith, and they said: Allah is enough for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs (3:173). Allah told the Prophet ﷺ: Allah is enough for you and for the believers who follow you (8:64). Against those who reject the truth, Allah will be enough for you (2:137).
The messengers delivered their message and feared no one but Allah, and Allah is enough as Reckoner (33:39). They did not need approval from the powerful, because their account was with Him.
trusting: Companies scramble before an audit; schools put on their best lessons the day the inspectors come. Al-Hasib's inspection is not one day a year. {idea}It is every moment, and nothing is hidden from the books.{/idea} A saying famously attributed to Umar ibn al-Khattab puts it simply: take account of yourselves before you are taken to account. A few honest minutes reviewing your day is a gift to your future self.

When you have been wronged, cheated or slandered, Al-Hasib means the account is still open with Him. {trap}Carrying every grudge until you can settle it yourself{/trap} poisons the heart. You can pursue your rights where that is fair, and still sleep, knowing He will balance every scale.
And when you are afraid of losing your job, your health or your support, say hasbunallah and mean it. {reward}The One who is enough has never failed anyone who truly relied on Him.{/reward}
loving: It is a rare thing to have someone who is enough, who fills the gap left by everyone and everything else. {idea}Al-Hasib is that for the heart that turns to Him.{/idea}
His reckoning is also a mercy: He counts the good generously, multiplies it, and forgives much. Loving Him grows from trusting that His account of you is fair and kind.
now: The landlord's message says the rent is going up, the job market is frozen, and your mind starts running numbers that do not add up. {reward}Say it slowly: hasbiyallah, Allah is enough for me.{/reward} Then do the next sensible thing, knowing the One who keeps every account will not leave yours unbalanced.
old: If I do not secure everything and settle every score, I will be left with nothing.
new: Al-Hasib keeps every account and is enough for me, so I can act calmly and let go of grudges.
try: Before sleeping tonight, spend three minutes reviewing your day honestly, then say hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil.

dua.text: Ya Hasib, You are enough for me. Take account of me with mercy, settle what I cannot settle, and make me content with You above all else.
dua.note: Call on Him by this name when you feel threatened, wronged or short of means; the believers said Allah is enough for us when they were told to fear (3:173).

pairs.why: Hasbunallah wa ni'mal wakil: Al-Hasib is enough for you, Al-Wakil takes charge of your affairs. Together they are the believer's full reliance (3:173).
Al-Muhsi counts every deed; Al-Hasib brings the count to a just reckoning.
Al-Hasib keeps the accounts and Al-Adl settles them with perfect justice, so no one is wronged by even a mustard seed.

faq.a: Al-Hasib has two connected meanings. Allah is the Reckoner who keeps precise account of every deed and will settle it with perfect justice, and He is the Sufficient, the One who is enough for whoever relies on Him.

faq.q: What does hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil mean?
faq.a: It means Allah is enough for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. The believers said it when they were told an army had gathered against them (3:173). Sahih al-Bukhari reports that Ibrahim said it when thrown into the fire, and the Prophet ﷺ said it on that occasion.

faq.q: What is the difference between Al-Hasib and Al-Muhsi?
faq.a: Al-Muhsi is the One who counts and records every single thing without missing any. Al-Hasib is the One who brings those records to account and settles them justly, and who is also sufficient for His servants. One keeps the record; the other reckons it and suffices.
